summary: The Title VIII Nursing Workforce Reauthorization Act of 2026 reauthorizes, revises, and establishes federal programs through fiscal year 2031 to support nursing education, recruitment, retention, and advanced practice nursing. The bill provides grant funding for increasing nursing school enrollment, expanding training in advanced technology and telehealth, supporting care for sexual assault survivors, and establishing temporary faculty salary-supplementation grants and regional nursing workforce data collection centers.

affected_groups.effect: Receive expanded access to scholarships, loan repayment programs, advanced practice training, and specialized instruction related to telehealth and sexual assault care.
Eligible for grants to increase enrollment capacity, purchase training technology, expand clinical partnerships, and participate in a temporary program to supplement faculty salaries.
Eligible to receive pilot program grants or contracts to establish or enhance state and regional nursing workforce centers and collect workforce data.
Benefit from targeted loan repayment and scholarship programs for nurses who agree to work in these facilities.

key_provisions: Reauthorizes and updates Health Resources and Services Administration nursing programs, including advanced education grants for nurse practitioners, nurse-midwives, nurse anesthetists, and clinical nurse specialists.
Expands training grants to cover new technologies such as telehealth, virtual laboratories, and simulation resources, and adds training for care of sexual assault survivors.
Establishes a temporary nurse faculty demonstration program to provide grants to accredited nursing schools to supplement eligible faculty salaries for up to three years.
Creates a three-year pilot program for state and regional nursing workforce centers to collect and report data, with matching fund requirements.
Authorizes appropriations of $184,337,000 for certain fiscal years under Section 871(a) and $121,135,000 under Section 871(b).

The bill provides grant funding for increasing nursing school enrollment, expanding training in advanced technology and telehealth, supporting care for sexual assault survivors, and establishing temporary faculty salary-supplementation grants and regional nursing workforce data collection centers.
summary_detail.significance: The bill impacts federal funding levels and administrative programs for the U.S. nursing workforce across multiple fiscal years through 2031, affecting nursing schools, healthcare facilities, students, and state agencies involved in health workforce planning.
